correctness.rationale: Exact two-arm and single-arm integrations prove the spline for every positive real length vector. Right density value gives L, initial slope gives unique k>=3. The signed distributional curvature peeling algorithm extracts the smallest unknown arm and its multiplicity because positive residual pairs are strictly larger. Induction proves all lengths recovered despite cancellations; k=1,2 give nonidentifiable interval splits. Exact independent rational verification passed 77483 tests.

originality.rationale: The complete population pair-distance distribution determines previously unknown positive arm lengths by the signed-curvature peeling theorem. Earlier general network-distance papers provide forward densities, not this inverse result. Published star configuration-persistence papers involve topological persistence, not scalar distance volume. Previously studied weighted-star first/second moments and unit-edge graph histograms do not imply this arbitrary-positive-length full inverse classification. Historical priority is provisional because not all unindexed inverse results can be excluded.
